title: pinout-openapi compatibility report (output DTO)
description: Machine-readable JSON report emitted on stdout (and, when settings.save_json_report, to settings.json_report_file) by `pinout-openapi validate`. Consumed by pinout-netlist/E2 for aggregation. Shape = report canon 1.1 (docs/report-format.md, the ecosystem-wide source of truth; decision record: pinout/debt/report-canon-fork.md, operator variant A, 2026-07-25). 1.1 is an ADDITIVE superset of the actually-frozen flat 1.0: it adds validator / interaction / consumer / generated_at / errors[].subject, and declares provenance the single source of provider identity. The process EXIT CODE (separate from this document) is fixed in x-exit-codes below. FROZEN: this is the sole output contract of the service.
x-canon: docs/report-format.md (canon 1.1; owner epic E1). Divergence from the canon is a defect of this file, not of the canon.
x-twin: pinout-asyncapi/api-specification/report.schema.json — known drift: the twin lists errors[].subject in items.required while its exit-3 envelope omits it (twin debt N1); this schema follows the canon (subject required for verdict codes, omitted for io/parse, hence not in items.required).

x-exit-codes.description: Canonical Result→exit mapping (cli-io grid, aligned with the twin pinout-asyncapi + operator decision OQ3). The exit code is the CLI's status line — the machine-readable serialization of the outcome; it is NOT a field of this report document. CONFIG_ERROR (exit 2) is a config-side breach detected before a report is written, so it never appears in errors[].code.

table.meaning: a verdict: the domain honestly said no (contract broken)
bad invocation / unreadable / schema-invalid config, or provider spec source not exactly-one
environment/spec: io or parse failure of an input artifact (consumed-contract or provider spec)

schema_version.description: Report-canon semver, so pinout-netlist can dispatch its reader by version. Bumped 1.0→1.1 by the additive canon delta (new fields: validator, interaction, consumer, generated_at, errors[].subject).

validator.description: Which validator produced this report (canon enum: pinout-openapi | pinout-asyncapi). A build-time constant, never a config value.

interaction.description: Interaction kind of the validated pair (canon enum: sync | async). A build-time constant.

consumer.description: Identity of the consuming side, from the consumer's own config (config.consumer.name). The report's only consumer-identity source.

version.description: OPTIONAL. Emitted only when actually known; never a placeholder. This validator has no source for it, so it is omitted entirely (never null or empty).

generated_at.description: When the report was produced. RFC 3339, UTC (Z), second precision, no fractional seconds, no offset. INJECTED FROM ABOVE through the clock port (D10) — the core never reads the system clock; the whole slice reads the clock exactly once (inside Reporter.Fold).

compatible.description: Aggregate verdict. Invariant: compatible ⇔ errors == []. true ⇒ exit 0; false ⇒ exit 1.

provenance.description: Top-level echo of the consumed-contract stamp (OQ5). The SINGLE source of provider identity in the canon — there is deliberately no separate provider{} block.

provider_version.description: Version stamp of the source spec.

captured_hash.description: sha256:… hash of the captured spec.

errors.description: All violations folded across operations (verdict codes F1–F4 at exit 1) and any input-side io/parse breach that produced a report (F6–F9 at exit 3). Empty ⇔ compatible. Flat list — grouping into verdicts[] is the rejected variant B; subject-level granularity is carried by errors[].subject.

code.description: Stable traceability key (FRD ↔ use-case ↔ contract). Verdict codes: OP_NOT_IN_PROVIDER (R1, F1), MISSING_REQUIRED_REQUEST_FIELD (R2, F2), READS_FIELD_NOT_PROVIDED (R3, F3), TYPE_MISMATCH (R4, F4) → exit 1. Io/parse codes: PARSE_ERROR (F6), FILE_NOT_FOUND (F7), HTTP_ERROR (F8), TIMEOUT_ERROR (F9) → exit 3. See x-exit-codes.

subject.description: What the violation is ABOUT — the graph-edge granularity pinout-netlist keys on (one subject = one edge). For verdict codes (exit 1) it is REQUIRED: the sync subject `METHOD /path` — uppercase method, one ASCII space, path byte-for-byte as recorded in the consumed contract (e.g. `GET /wallets/{id}`). It is the PREFIX of location, extracted from the same single computation, never composed a second time by hand. For io/parse codes (exit 3) there is no operation/channel identified, so the key is omitted.

location.description: `METHOD PATH` (the subject) plus the field/parameter, when applicable. Always starts with the subject.

uncovered_operations.description: Informational only (FRD F5d): provider operations outside consumer.operations. No effect on the verdict or the exit code.
